title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its node values level by level from left to right.
inputFormat: First line: integer n, the number of level-order tokens
Second line: n space-separated values, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print one level per line with values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: The tree contains only its root.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it is a valid binary search tree. Every node in the left subtree must be strictly smaller and every node in the right subtree strictly greater than the node.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print true if the tree is a valid BST; otherwise print false.

examples.explanation: Both children satisfy the strict BST ordering.
The value 3 lies in the right subtree of 5 but is smaller than 5.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of BST
description: Given a binary search tree and two distinct node values p and q, return the value of their lowest common ancestor.
inputFormat: Third line: integers p and q
outputFormat: Print the value of the lowest common ancestor.
constraints: p and q exist in the tree

examples.explanation: Nodes 2 and 8 lie on opposite sides of 6.
A node may be an ancestor of itself.

title: Path Sum II
description: Given a binary tree and a target sum, return every root-to-leaf path whose node values add up to the target. Preserve left-to-right traversal order.
outputFormat: First print the number of paths, then print one path per line.

examples.explanation: Both displayed root-to-leaf paths sum to 22.

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the values visible when the tree is viewed from its right side, ordered from top to bottom.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print the visible values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: The rightmost nodes at the three levels are 1, 3, and 4.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description: Design serialization and deserialization for a binary tree. Serialize the tree to a comma-separated preorder string using # for null children. Deserializing that string must reconstruct the original tree.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print the canonical preorder serialization with commas and # null markers.

examples.explanation: Preorder traversal records both values and null child positions.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: A path in a binary tree is a sequence of connected nodes in which each adjacent pair is joined by an edge. A node may appear at most once, and the path does not need to pass through the root. Return the maximum sum along any path.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children

title: Recover Binary Search Tree
description: Exactly two nodes in a binary search tree were swapped by mistake. Restore the tree without changing its structure.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens representing the corrupted BST
outputFormat: Print the inorder traversal of the restored BST.
constraints: Exactly two node values are swapped

examples.explanation: Swapping values 1 and 3 restores the BST.

title: Vertical Order Traversal
description: Return the vertical order traversal of a binary tree. Nodes are grouped by column from left to right; within a column they are ordered by row, then by value when row and column are equal.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print one vertical column per line with values separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Columns are emitted from horizontal position -1 through 2.

title: Binary Tree Cameras
description: Place cameras on tree nodes so every node is monitored. A camera monitors its parent, itself, and its immediate children. Return the minimum number of cameras required.
inputFormat: Second line: n level-order tokens, using null for missing children
outputFormat: Print the minimum number of cameras.

examples.explanation: One camera on the second node monitors every node.
Two cameras are needed for this chain.
